- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — apply a 1-2 day lag correction downward.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3-5 day horizons: if forecast is 2-3% above recent 7-day average, adjust down; if below, adjust up.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently fails to capture long-term sentiment-driven drift — if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5-1.5% to forecast; if downward, subtract 0.5-1.5%.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment shifts sharply, wait 2-3 days before adjusting forecast; use 3-day moving average sentiment as filter.
